title: A body in a changing field: gradient seen, fall from rest, level dependence

key_results.statement:
Gradient seen: $\gamma(\lambda)=\langle\varphi\vert e^{iC_f\lambda}Ye^{-iC_f\lambda}\vert\varphiangle=\sum_
u\hat\gamma_
u e^{i
u\lambda}$, a real trigonometric polynomial in the field frequencies $
u$; it is constant iff $\hat\gamma_
u=0$ for every $
u
eq0$ (always for $Y=y\,\mathbb 1_f$).

For every $C_f$, $Y$, $\varphi$ and every start, the first-order term of the view of $\{b,c\}$ and of every schedule of readings depends on the field only through the real function $\gamma$ on $[0,\lambda]$ (exact first-order coefficient); the second order is not a function of $\gamma$.

The generator $C_{\rm eff}(\lambda)=C_{br}+\gamma(\lambda)\,\hat x\otimes G\otimes\mathbb 1_c$ reproduces the view and every schedule up to $O(\lVert Y\rVert^2)$; it is the contract of an admissible description iff $\gamma$ is constant, which can hold for a field that is not stationary (under (2.11) of 02-field-object, for $[Y,C_f]=0$, for $Y=y\,\mathbb 1_f$); it is exact at all orders for a sharp stationary field and under (2.11) of 02-field-object.

Sharp start with (2.11) of 02-field-object violated: $1-\operatorname{Tr}V(\lambda)^2=\frac{\lambda^4}{2}\Gamma\lVert(Y-\gamma)C_f\varphi\rVert^2+O(\lambda^5)$, so the view first differs from that of the generator at order $Y^2$ and $\lambda^4$ if $(Y-\gamma)C_f\varphi\neq0$ and $\Gamma\neq0$ (at $Y^2$ and $\lambda^{2k_0+2}$ if (2.11) first fails at $k_0>1$; the $\lambda^4$ coefficient vanishes if $\Gamma=0$); under (2.11) there is no difference at any order.

First-order velocity of a branch start $B_{k,\sigma}[g]$: $v^{(1)}_g(\lambda)=\int_0^\lambda\mathrm ds\,\gamma(s)\,\mathcal K_g(\lambda,s)$, for every level, branch, smooth $g$ and continuous $\gamma$, at $\kappa\to0$, $\langle X\rangle=0$ (exact first-order coefficient); for constant $\gamma$ it reduces to (4.7) of 04-branch-fall.

Kernel: $\mathcal K_g(\lambda,s)=\langle k_0+k_1\cos(2\omega(\lambda-s))\rangle_g-2\sigma M^2\int\frac{\mathrm dp}{2\pi}\frac{\omega'}{\omega}\sin(2\omega(\lambda-s))[j_g+\sigma\lambda\omega'\lvert g\rvert^2]$ with $k_0=-M^2\omega''/\omega$, $k_1=-M^2\tau^2(M^2+\tau^2)\sin^2p/\omega^4$; it depends on $\lvert g\rvert^2$ and on the position density $j_g$.

Every smooth $g$ at rest: $\lvert\mathcal K_g(\lambda,s)-K_{\chi_g}(\lambda-s)\rvert\le4\tau^2(u+\tau^2\lambda/M)(\delta p^2+2\rho_g)$ with $K_\chi(\Delta)=-\tau^2[1+\sigma\chi\sin(2M_k\Delta)]$; in the limit (I), $\delta p\to0$ at fixed $\lambda$, of the class $\mathcal S_\chi$ the kernel is $K_\chi$.

Limit (I) of the class $\mathcal S_\chi$, any continuous $\gamma$: $v^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)=-\tau^2\int_0^\lambda\mathrm ds\,\gamma(s)[1+\sigma\chi\sin(2M_k(\lambda-s))]$ and $a^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)=-\tau^2\gamma(\lambda)-2\sigma\chi M_k\tau^2\int_0^\lambda\mathrm ds\,\gamma(s)\cos(2M_k(\lambda-s))$, each derived from its own kernel.

Exact bound for the acceleration of every smooth $g$ at rest: $\lvert a^{(1)}_g(\lambda)-a_{\chi_g}(\lambda)\rvert\le\tau^2\sup_{[0,\lambda]}\lvert\gamma\rvert(1+4M\lambda)(u+2\tau^2\lambda/M)(\delta p^2+2\rho_g)$.

Ranges of a fixed start, each sufficient and taken from the exact bound of its own quantity ($E_v$ for the velocity, $E_a$ for the acceleration), with $w_g=\delta p^2+2\rho_g$, $\Gamma_\lambda=\sup_{[0,\lambda]}\lvert\gamma\rvert$, $\lambda_g=M/(\tau^2w_g)$, $\lambda_a=\min\{1/(Mu\,w_g),1/(\tau\sqrt{w_g})\}\le\lambda_g$: the drift of the velocity for $u\,w_g\ll\lvert\gamma_0\rvert/\Gamma_\lambda$ and $\lambda\ll(\lvert\gamma_0\rvert/\Gamma_\lambda)\lambda_g$; the part of frequency $\Omega$ of the velocity, against $\tau^2\lvert\gamma_1\rvert/\Omega$, for $4\Omega\lambda(u+\tau^2\lambda/M)w_g\ll\lvert\gamma_1\rvert/\Gamma_\lambda$; the acceleration, against $\tau^2\Gamma_\lambda$, for $u\,w_g\ll1$ and $\lambda\ll\lambda_a$; the conditions of the drift do not imply $\lambda\ll\lambda_a$ where $\lvert\gamma_0\rvert/\Gamma_\lambda>\lambda_a/\lambda_g$, for which $\lvert\gamma_0\rvert/\Gamma_\lambda>\tau\sqrt{w_g}/M$ is sufficient.

Limit (I), class $\mathcal S_\chi$, $\gamma=\gamma_0+\gamma_1\cos(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)$, $\Omega\neq2M_k$: the velocity is the drift $-\tau^2\gamma_0\lambda$ (the only growing part of the limit function) plus a part of frequency $\Omega$, $-\tau^2\gamma_1[\sin(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)/\Omega+\sigma\chi\,2M_k\cos(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)/(4M_k^2-\Omega^2)]$, a part of frequency $2M_k$ proportional to $\chi$, and a constant.

Limit (I), class $\mathcal S_\chi$, $\Omega\neq2M_k$: $a^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}=-\tau^2\gamma_0-\tau^2\gamma_1[\cos(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)-\sigma\chi\frac{2M_k\Omega\sin(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)}{4M_k^2-\Omega^2}]$ plus a part of frequency $2M_k$ proportional to $\chi$; the limit acceleration has no growing part.

Response at the field frequency in the limit (I): $\mathcal A_{k,\sigma}(\Omega)=-\tau^2[1+i\sigma\chi\,2M_k\Omega/(4M_k^2-\Omega^2)]$ for $\Omega\neq2M_k$; it tends to $-\tau^2$, i.e. (4.16) of 04-branch-fall per unit gradient, for $\Omega\to0$; for one class $\mathcal S_\chi$ on all levels and $\Omega>0$ different from all $2M_k$, $\mathcal A_{k,\sigma}(\Omega)$ is the same for all levels iff $\chi=0$; leading level dependence $-i\sigma\chi\tau^2\Omega/2M_k$ for $\Omega\ll2M_k$.

Resonance $\Omega=2M_k$, limit (I) of $\mathcal S_\chi$: the limit velocity of the level $k$ has the growing oscillation $-\sigma\chi\tau^2\gamma_1\frac\lambda2\sin(2M_k\lambda+\vartheta)$ and the limit acceleration $-\sigma\chi\tau^2\gamma_1M_k\lambda\cos(2M_k\lambda+\vartheta)$; in the limit (I) no level with $2M_{k'}\neq\Omega$ has a growing oscillation, and none for $\chi=0$; a fixed start has the growing part of the velocity, with $\chi=\chi_g$, if $u\,w_g\ll\lvert\chi_g\gamma_1\rvert/\Gamma_\lambda$ and $\lambda\ll(\lvert\chi_g\gamma_1\rvert/\Gamma_\lambda)\lambda_g$, and that of the acceleration under the same two conditions together with $M\lambda\ge1$ (sufficient); the parts that do not grow have sufficient ranges of their own: $8M\lambda(u+\tau^2\lambda/M)w_g\ll\lvert\gamma_1\rvert/\Gamma_\lambda$ for the velocity, against the amplitude $\tau^2\lvert\gamma_1\rvert/2M_k$, and $u\,w_g\ll1$, $\lambda\ll\lambda_a$ for the acceleration, against $\tau^2\Gamma_\lambda$.

Order (II), fixed smooth start, $\lambda	o\infty$, every $\Omega>0$: $v^{(1)}_g=\lambda\{\gamma_0\langle\alpha_0angle_g+\gamma_1\operatorname{Re}[c_g(\Omega)e^{i(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)}]\}+o(\lambda)$; the oscillation of frequency $\Omega$ grows like $\lambda$ where $\gamma_1c_g(\Omega)

eq0$ at one of the labels with $2\omega_k(p)=\Omega$, and $c_g(\Omega)=0$ for particular starts that vanish at all of them; after $\delta p	o0$ at rest $c_g	o-	au^2$ at $\Omega=2M_k$ and $c_g	o0$ for $\Omega<2M_k$ and for $\Omega\ge2\sqrt{M_k^2+	au^2}$, for every sequence, and $c_g	o0$ for $2M_k<\Omega<2\sqrt{M_k^2+	au^2}$ along sequences vanishing near $\{p:2\omega_k(p)=\Omega\}$ (not determined for other sequences); the orders (I) and (II) do not commute at $\Omega=2M_k$.

Real start at rest at resonance, exact for all $\lambda\ge0$: the acceleration is $-\tau^2\gamma(\lambda)-2\gamma_1\lambda^2\langle M^2\omega'^2\frac{\sin\eta\lambda}{\eta\lambda}\cos((\omega+M)\lambda+\vartheta)\rangle_g$ plus a rest bounded by $\tau^2u\lvert\gamma_1\rvert(1+5M\lambda)q_g$, and the velocity has the analogous form; before dephasing the finite-width terms are $-(\tau^4\gamma_1q_g/M)\lambda^2\sin(2M_k\lambda+\vartheta)$ and $-2\tau^4\gamma_1q_g\lambda^2\cos(2M_k\lambda+\vartheta)$, of relative size one, against the amplitudes $\tau^2\lvert\gamma_1\rvert/2M$ and $\tau^2\lvert\gamma_1\rvert$ of the sharp-label velocity and acceleration, at $\lambda=1/(\tau\sqrt{2q_g})\ll\lambda_g$; for $\lambda\to\infty$ it becomes (12.15).

Distance from the quasistatic value, limit (I), one class $\mathcal S_\chi$, exact: $\lvert\mathcal A_{k,\sigma}(\Omega)+\tau^2\rvert\le\delta\tau^2$ for all levels iff $\Omega\notin\bigcup_k(\Omega^{(k)}_-,\Omega^{(k)}_+)$, $\Omega^{(k)}_\mp=\frac{M_k}{\delta}(\sqrt{\chi^2+4\delta^2}\mp\lvert\chi\rvert)$; this is not the criterion for agreement between the levels.

Level spread of the response at the field frequency, normalized by $\tau^2$, for $\Omega$ different from every $2M_k$ with $\chi_k\neq0$: $\mathcal D(\Omega)=\max_kc_kh_k-\min_kc_kh_k$ with $c_k=\sigma_k\chi_k$, $h_k=2M_k\Omega/(4M_k^2-\Omega^2)$; the response is the same for all levels to the relative accuracy $\delta$ iff $\mathcal D(\Omega)\le\delta$; for one class and one branch, (12.16) at $\delta/2$ is sufficient at every $\Omega$, and (12.16) at $\delta$ is sufficient for $\Omega<2M_0$ or $\Omega>2M_{N-1}$ and necessary for $2M_0<\Omega<2M_{N-1}$; if both branches of all levels are compared in one class, (12.16) at $\delta/2$ is necessary and sufficient; exceptional members: $\chi=0$, nearly equal level data, $\Omega$ at or near a $2M_k$.

One class and one branch, $\Omega<2M_0$ or $\Omega>2M_{N-1}$: $\mathcal D(\Omega)=\lvert\chi\rvert\frac{2\Omega(M_{N-1}-M_0)(4M_0M_{N-1}+\Omega^2)}{(4M_0^2-\Omega^2)(4M_{N-1}^2-\Omega^2)}$; for $0<\Omega<2m$, $\mathcal D(\Omega)\le\delta$ iff $\Omega\le\Omega_\delta$ with $\Omega_\delta=\frac{2\delta}{\lvert\chi\rvert}\frac{M_0M_{N-1}}{M_{N-1}-M_0}(1+O(\Omega_\delta^2/m^2))$.

Complete acceleration in the limit (I), every continuous $\gamma$: $a^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)=-\tau^2\gamma(\lambda)+\sigma\chi R_k[\gamma](\lambda)$, $R_k[\gamma]=-2M_k\tau^2\int_0^\lambda\mathrm ds\,\gamma(s)\cos(2M_k(\lambda-s))$; for $\gamma\not\equiv0$ it is the same for all levels iff $\chi_k=0$ on every level; to the accuracy $\delta$ only a sufficient condition is derived: for $\gamma=\gamma_0+\gamma_1\cos(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)$ and $\Omega$ different from every $2M_k$, $2\max_k\lvert\chi_k\rvert\frac{2M_k+\Omega}{\lvert2M_k-\Omega\rvert}\le\delta$ is sufficient for the complete accelerations of all levels and both branches to agree within $\delta\tau^2(\lvert\gamma_0\rvert+\lvert\gamma_1\rvert)$ at every $\lambda\ge0$; its average over a window of length $\Lambda$ is $-\tau^2\gamma_0+O(1/\Lambda)$ for all levels if $\Omega\neq2M_k$.

Two-place field with $Y=y\lvert1\rangle\langle1\rvert$, $\varphi=\lvert0\rangle$: $\gamma(\lambda)=y\sin^2(\gamma_f\lambda)$, i.e. $\gamma_0=y/2$, $\gamma_1=-y/2$, $\Omega=2\lvert\gamma_f\rvert$, $\vartheta=0$; for $y\neq0$ the field is sharp and not stationary and $C_{\rm eff}(\lambda)$ is not a contract; for $y=0$ the body sees no field, $\gamma\equiv0$ and $C_{\rm eff}=C_{br}$ is a contract.

open_issues: Between the orders (I) and (II) only (12.19) is derived, for a real start at resonance; a formula uniform in λ for starts with j_g ≠ 0, or through δp and χ_g alone, is not derived; the exact (12.6), (12.7) cover it implicitly.

The ranges of (12.18) and of Result 3(b) are sufficient and rest on the bounds E_v, E_a, which are uniform in γ; whether a fixed start is described beyond them is not derived, except by the exact (12.19) for a real start at resonance; for a γ without a frequency near 2M_k the acceleration may be described on a longer range than λ_a, which is not derived.
For the complete acceleration only the exact-equality criterion and a sufficient condition for the accuracy δ are derived (12.22); a necessary and sufficient condition for the accuracy δ is not.

Order (II) for a field frequency inside the band, 2M_k < Ω < 2√(M_k² + τ²): the limit δp → 0 of c_g(Ω) depends on the weight of the starts near the labels with 2ω_k(p) = Ω and is evaluated only for sequences that vanish near these labels; for a fixed start that vanishes at all these labels c_g(Ω) is real and can vanish (control of Step 9), which of these starts have c_g(Ω) = 0 is not characterized, and where γ_1 c_g(Ω) = 0 only the estimate o(λ) of (12.15) is derived for the part of frequency Ω of the velocity.
Sequences at rest with ρ_g not tending to zero belong to no class S_χ; for them only (12.6), (12.7) and the bounds (12.8), (12.10), (12.18) are available.
The growth at Ω = 2M_k is a statement on the first-order coefficient at each fixed λ; the range of λ in which it is the leading effect needs the second order in Y, which is outside the scope.

consistency_checks.check: Constant γ: (12.6), (12.7) give the growing part of (4.7) of 04-branch-fall with G_k = γ M_k, and at rest (12.9) has the window average −τ²γ of (4.16).
A gradient pulse evaluated by an independent route (label shift inside the branch plus the amplitude on the other branch) reproduces the sharp-label kernel of (12.8).
Dimensions: velocities are costs, accelerations and the kernel are costs squared, γ, χ, δ and (12.5) are pure numbers.
